headline_marked: 90 hurt as [[Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash]] at 4 campuses
headline: 90 hurt as Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash at 4 campuses
summary: Violence erupted at Jagannath University, Dhaka College, and Govt Madrasa-e-Alia, with clashes continuing into the hospital where injured students were treated.
details: Clashes between Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir activists erupted at three educational institutions in Dhaka on Tuesday, marking the largest confrontation since the July mass uprising.
The violence began at Jagannath University around 12 PM and quickly spread to Dhaka College and the Government Madrasa-e-Alia, leaving over 50 people injured in the city alone.

At Jagannath University, the conflict started during a documentary screening. Tensions rose when activists from the JNU Student Union (JAKSU), Chhatra Shakti, and Inkilab Manch attempted to enter the hall with placards to demand a second campus and better medical services.

According to witnesses, the clash escalated when Chhatra Dal activists attacked a Shibir leader at the university's Shaheed Minar. The violence then spread to the university's medical center, where Shibir activists had sought refuge.
The violence extended beyond the campus. Injured Shibir and Chhatra Shakti activists were attacked twice more at the Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital while receiving treatment.
A doctor at the hospital reported that at least 50 people received treatment for head injuries, with four to five patients transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for critical care.
Similar clashes were also reported on Monday at Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur, bringing the total number of campuses hit by violence in two days to four.
The tension stems from recent student union elections where Shibir-backed panels won most positions in five major universities, while Chhatra Dal performed poorly, leading to ongoing rivalry.

headline_marked: 6 [[Naya Dhara leaders taken into custody]] after Press Club clash
headline: 6 Naya Dhara leaders taken into custody after Press Club clash
summary: Police detained six leaders following a clash between Naya Dhara and Rashtra Sanglap Forum that disrupted emergency services at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
details: Police took six leaders and activists of Naya Dhara Bangladesh into custody Tuesday night following a clash with members of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum near the Jatiya Press Club and a subsequent standoff at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The detainees include Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi, Senior Vice-Chairman Shanta Farzana, and other senior leaders. They were escorted out of the hospital's emergency department under police protection around 11:10 pm.

The conflict began Tuesday evening during a Naya Dhara protest near the Press Club regarding an alleged assault on Shanta Farzana on August 1. Several people from both sides were injured and taken to DMCH for treatment.

Following the initial clash, supporters of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum allegedly confined Naya Dhara leaders inside the emergency department for three hours, disrupting medical services for approximately 90 minutes.

Rashtra Sanglap Forum leaders claimed that Naya Dhara activists attacked them after Shanta Farzana made offensive remarks about July fighters and the BNP. Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi alleged that the forum members attacked first and stole journalists' phones.
Inspector Md Faruk of the DMCH police camp stated that the disorder caused significant fear among patients and their attendants before police intervened to restore order.
